label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging only 0.81, PHQ-9 depression scores at 0.32, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near zero (0.04), these individuals demonstrate strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions. They spend a moderate 1–3 hours of daily screen or online time, suggesting balanced digital habits.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily usage
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores indicating strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology well below clinical thresholds
Near-zero anxiety levels suggesting effective emotional regulation
Moderate daily screen/online time (1–3 hours) reflecting balanced digital engagement
Higher educational attainment potentially linked to greater coping resources
tone: Stable, socially connected, and psychologically resilient

label: High-Distress Heavy-Screen-Time Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on screens and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score averages 1.72, PHQ-9 depression score averages 1.76, and GAD-7 anxiety score averages 2.18, all indicating consistently higher psychological distress across all three dimensions. With 176 respondents in the training split, this is a sizable cluster characterized by co-occurring mental health challenges.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily screen time
behavior_markers: Exhibits the highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.18)
Engages in prolonged daily screen use exceeding 5 hours
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggests compounding distress

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
